summary: Intermittent edge POP route flap causing long-tail inference p95 and streaming timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-09 21:00 UTC, a subset of requests from Mailboxly (dedicated account) to hosted endpoints are experiencing increased p95/p99 latencies and occasional streaming timeouts. The error pattern shows long-tail token emission stalls followed by request timeouts (client sees HTTP 504/stream disconnect).

Impact: Affects ~5% of Mailboxly production inference traffic routed through the us-west POP; degraded user experience for chat features, increased client-side retries, and duplicated billing events observed. No complete region outage.

Environment: prod; us-west POP (edge cluster usw-pop-17). Dedicated pool: dp-usw-mailboxly. Models in use: redwood-7b-v2 and community-llm-13b pinned in the customer's rollout.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send chat-streaming request via customer API key to the redwood streaming endpoint from an IP traceable to Mailboxly's CIDR. 2) Observe response stream; after 10-60s tokens may pause, then connection drops or client receives 504. 3) Repeating with same client from different region (us-east) does not reproduce.

Observed behavior: p50 stable, p95 and p99 increased by 3-9x for affected traces; frequent streaming stall pattern where KV cache hits continue but no outbound tokens emitted; server side shows active inference threads stuck in "waiting-for-egress-ack" state.

Expected behavior: steady token emission with p95 within SLA (200-600ms per-client-turn depending on model) and no streaming disconnects for sustained sessions.

Initial logs & hashes: Request trace IDs evidence in customer logs: trace-20260309-usw-0001..0007. Edge proxy (usw-pop-17) logs show repeated 502->200->timeout sequences for same upstream host IPs. No model OOMs reported in serving runtime.

Additional notes: Customer first raised via support chat; elevated to P1 due to production impact and billing anomalies from client retries.
steps_to_reproduce: Issue is intermittent; reproduce reliably by sending sustained streaming session (>30s) from Mailboxly's IPs routed through us-west.
Run curl against streaming endpoint with chunked transfer to simulate typing pattern and observe stall after multiple tokens.
Compare runs from us-east and us-west to confirm regional skew.
logs: edge/usw-pop-17/proxy.log: 2026-03-09T21:12:07Z downstream=10.12.45.22 upstream=18.205.34.22 response=502 then 200 then timeout
serving-runtime/dp-usw-mailboxly/instance-3/kernel.log: no OOMs; threads show KV cache active; thread stack shows wait at net_send() in proxy client library
comments: 2026-03-09 22:05 - Support (Aisha): Logged case after customer reported repeated streaming stalls; assigned to SRE for initial triage.
2026-03-09 23:40 - SRE (Jin): Confirmed increased latency spikes on us-west POP; beginning packet captures at edge and upstream egress gateway.
2026-03-10 01:15 - Customer (Mailboxly): Provided pcap and example trace IDs; notes issue correlates with peak 20:30-22:00 PDT traffic.
2026-03-10 08:30 - Networking (Carlos Mendes): Observed intermittent BGP path change events to the POP resulting in asymmetric return path for a subset of client IPs.
2026-03-11 11:20 - SRE (Jin): Deployed temporary routing rule to force affinity to healthy egress node; observed reduction in stalled streams for affected requests.
2026-03-12 09:02 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed degradation reduced but still seeing occasional stalls; holding P1 pending permanent mitigation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge-to-egress asymmetric routing causing the upstream ACKs to be dropped or delayed; server's streaming library waits on ACK from proxy before sending next chunk -> long stalls.

Hypothesis 2: Healthcheck flapping on one NLB target group in us-west causing intermittent traffic to be sent to a degraded instance that partially accepts requests (200) but fails to keep TCP keepalive, leading to downstream stalls.
Finding: BGP churn timestamps line up with increased counts of retransmit and out-of-order packets in packet captures (pcap id pc-usw-03).

Temporary mitigation: Applied a static egress affinity policy for Mailboxly traffic (route via egress-set-2) and enabled more aggressive TCP keepalive on edge proxies. Result: p95 improved from 3.2s to 740ms for a sample window.
Observed side-effect: Some client IPs that previously routed to a closer POP were forced to a different egress, increasing TTFB for warm sessions; tradeoff accepted to restore stream continuity.
resolution_notes:
Workaround: Persistent route affinity applied for Mailboxly to egress-set-2 and aggressive keepalive settings on the edge proxies rolled out to usw-pop-17. Permanent fix: Networking to collaborate with infra to tune NLB healthcheck origin consistency and deploy control-plane change to stabilize BGP communities on the us-west edges.

Rollout notes: Change deployed to usw-pop-17 on 2026-03-11 14:00 UTC with verification window 48h. Post-mitigation metrics show p95 reduction and streaming disconnect count reduced by ~86% for Mailboxly.

Follow-ups: (1) Networking to add synthetic egress health probes that mimic streaming traffic patterns (owner: Carlos Mendes, due 2026-03-19). (2) SRE to add alert for "waiting-for-egress-ack" thread states (owner: Jin Park, due 2026-03-15). (3) Reach out to Mailboxly CS to review retry/backoff behavior to reduce duplicate billing (owner: Aisha Patel, due 2026-03-13).
